Thought: Alkali metals are the elements in Group 1 of the periodic table (lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, cesium, and francium). I need to recall their characteristic reaction with water. Alkali metals are highly reactive and when they come into contact with water, they undergo a vigorous reaction. They donate their single valence electron easily, reacting with water to produce hydrogen gas and a metal hydroxide. The reaction is exothermic (produces heat) and becomes more violent as you move down the group. For example, sodium reacts vigorously with water, producing hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide, while potassium reacts even more violently. The general reaction is: 2M + 2H₂O → 2MOH + H₂ (where M is the alkali metal).

Looking at the options:
A. Moderately, producing some bubbling - This understates the reaction
B. Non-reactive - This is incorrect; alkali metals are highly reactive with water
C. Slowly, producing little heat - This understates the reaction
D. Violently and rapidly, producing heat and hydrogen gas - This correctly describes the reaction
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
